answer: An auditor observes that every claim is sealed in a walnut shell at submission and opened only at settlement, each shell carrying a saffron stamp from an auditor with no interaction that epoch with the claimant. The stamp is cipher-sealed, so a claimant cannot learn which auditor opens the shell; pairing is drawn at settlement from the roster. A farm pre-purchasing auditors buys stamps that attach to random shells, not its own. Violations are stamped shells whose contents contradict the record, and both claimant and stamp forfeit emission.
